title: A sandwich enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay for the quantitation of human plasma ferritin
author: Bleicher, Unger, et al.
materials: were coated with 100 μl/well goat anti-ferritin polyclonal antibody (Abcam ab

steps.title: Coat plates with capture antibody
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL per well of goat anti‑ferritin polyclonal antibody (Abcam ab33574) diluted to 367 ng/mL in PBS to Nunc MaxiSorp® flat‑bottom 96‑well plates (ThermoFisher Scientific 442404) and incubate overnight at 4 °C.

steps.title: Wash and block wells
steps.instruction: Wash wells with wash buffer (0.05 % Tween‑20 in PBS). Then add 200 µL per well of reagent diluent (1 % BSA (Sigma A7906) and 0.05 % Tween‑20 in PBS) and incubate 1 h at room temperature.

steps.title: Add samples and standards
steps.instruction: After washing, add 100 µL per well of either human plasma diluted 1:8 in reagent diluent or ferritin standards prepared from Liquichek Immunology Control L3 (BIORAD 596) diluted 1:4 in reagent diluent then serially diluted 1:2 over 10 points; aliquot each in duplicate and incubate 2 h at room temperature.

steps.title: Add biotinylated detection antibody
steps.instruction: Wash wells, then add 100 µL per well of biotinylated rabbit anti‑ferritin polyclonal antibody (Abcam ab7333) diluted to 125 ng/mL in reagent diluent and incubate 1 h at room temperature.

steps.title: Add streptavidin‑HRP
steps.instruction: Wash wells, then add 100 µL per well of streptavidin‑horseradish peroxidase (Abcam ab7403) diluted to 67 ng/mL in reagent diluent and incubate 1 h at room temperature.

steps.title: Develop with TMB substrate
steps.instruction: Wash wells, add 100 µL per well of 3,3′,5,5′‑tetramethylbenzidine (TMB) substrate (BD 555214). Incubate 30 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Stop reaction and read plate
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL per well of 1 M H₂SO₄ stop solution, then measure absorbance at 450 nm using a FLUOstar Omega microplate reader (BMG LABTECH).

steps.title: Generate standard curve
steps.instruction: Create a standard curve from the measured standards and extrapolate ferritin concentrations for the unknown plasma samples.

steps.title: Determine optimal antibody concentrations
steps.instruction: Perform checkerboard titrations using a plasma pool, testing capture antibody from 0.2 to 11 µg/mL and detection antibody from 0.125 to 5 µg/mL; select the lowest concentrations that give a clear standard curve and accurately quantify test plasma samples (13, 27, 54 ng/mL ferritin).

steps.title: Assess assay sensitivity
steps.instruction: Measure seven ferritin standards ranging from 0.88 to 0.028 ng/mL in ten independent assays and compare to a no‑ferritin control to determine assay sensitivity.

steps.title: Compare ELISA to commercial assay
steps.instruction: Analyze twenty‑one plasma samples using the ARCHITECT Ferritin chemiluminescent immunoassay (Melbourne Health Shared Pathology Service, Royal Melbourne Hospital) and compare the results to those obtained with the in‑house ELISA.

steps.title: Evaluate intra‑ and inter‑assay precision
steps.instruction: Include two plasma samples with known low and normal ferritin concentrations in seventeen assays over four months to assess inter‑assay consistency; additionally, measure two samples six times within a single assay to evaluate intra‑assay variation.
